title: Unnati Hooda Exits French Open After Three-Game Defeat
indian_angle: Indian shuttler Unnati Hooda's performance at the French Open is a key focus for fans following her international progress.
summary: Unnati Hooda was defeated by Japan’s Riko Gunji in the women’s singles first round of the French Open 2026 in a closely contested three-game match.

title: Satwik-Chirag Out of French Open; Asmita, Tanvi Advance
indian_angle: India's top men's doubles pair faced an early exit, while two women's singles players continued their run at the French Open.
summary: World No. 5 Indian pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty lost to France's Popov brothers, while Asmita Chaliha and Tanvi Sharma secured their spots in the next round of the French Open.

title: BAI Releases Minutes of Junior Selection Committee Meeting
indian_angle: This update provides transparency on the selection process for India's junior badminton players, directly impacting their career paths.
summary: The Badminton Association of India (BAI) published the minutes from its recent Junior Selection Committee meeting held on October 19, 2026.

title: BAI Announces Formation of New Athletes Committee
indian_angle: The formation of this committee by BAI ensures greater athlete representation and input in the governance of Indian badminton.
summary: Badminton Association of India (BAI) officially announced the formation of its new Athletes Committee on October 2, 2026, aimed at empowering players.

title: Junior World Championships Coaching Camp Underway in Guwahati
indian_angle: This camp is crucial for preparing India's young talents for the upcoming BWF World Junior Championships, nurturing future stars.
summary: A national coaching camp for the BWF World Junior Championships 2026 is being held at the National Center of Excellence (NCE) in Guwahati, focusing on junior player development.

title: BAI Level-1 Advanced Coaches Course Held in Guwahati & Raipur
indian_angle: The course enhances the quality of coaching available to Indian badminton players, contributing to long-term talent development.
summary: The Badminton Association of India conducted a Level-1 (Advanced) Coaches Course at NCE Guwahati and Raipur from September 14 to 23, 2026, to upskill national coaches.
